Body, health & movement

tickle verb and noun

also tickling, ticklish

classical

Lucr. 2.429
Cic. Fin. 1.39

tītillō, tītillāre

verb, first conjugation, transitive

Classical writers mostly use the verb of pleasure tickling the senses.

Examples

  • praecipua hilaritātis sēdēs, quod tītillātū maximē intellegitur ālārum

    [the diaphragm is] the chief seat of laughter, as tickling the armpits shows bestPlin. NH 11.198

  • Tītillābō tē!

    I’m going to tickle you!composed

  • Ubi tītillem? Sub ālīs?

    Where shall I tickle you? Under your arms?composed

  • Nōlī mē tītillāre!

    Don’t tickle me!composed

Other words

  • tītillātiō, tītillātiōnis f. — tickling

    noun, third declension · classical · Cic. N.D. 1.113; Cic. Sen. 47; Sen. Ep. 92.6

  • tītillātus, tītillātūs m. — tickling

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Plin. NH 11.198

See also hiccup.

SourcesLewis & Short: titillo · Lewis & Short: titillatio · Lewis & Short: titillatus
